It's genuinely encouraging that you want to change this—that awareness is already a meaningful first step, and it says a lot about you.

One approach that helps many people is starting small rather than forcing big positive thoughts. At the end of each day, try noting just one thing that went okay, even something minor like a decent cup of coffee. You might also gently notice negative thoughts without judging yourself for them, then ask whether they're fully true or just a habit your mind has fallen into. Being kind to yourself in the process matters more than getting it "right."

If this negativity feels heavy, persistent, or is affecting your daily life or mood, it could be worth talking with a therapist or counselor, who can help you build lasting tools. And if you ever notice thoughts turning into hopelessness or self-harm, please reach out to a crisis line or someone you trust right away. Change is possible, and you don't have to figure it out alone.
